ns2:section.sectionText: Students will learn about variations in conceptions of human rights both across time and across cultures, and the challenges these variations present for defending human rights at the global scale. Subsequently, we will cover and critique the international infrastructure aimed at defining and protecting human rights, including international law, the United Nations, the International Criminal Court, humanitarian military intervention, and non-governmental organizations. Throughout the semester, students will conduct independent research on a humanitarian crisis of their choosing and present their findings in a variety of formats.
